departure_points.name: Town of 1770 public boat ramp and pontoon, Captain Cook Drive
departure_points.detail: State-owned recreational ramp (facility MV21) with a pontoon on Round Hill Creek, managed by Gladstone Regional Council. Recently upgraded, with parking; launching is easy but tide timing is critical.

departure_points.name: 1770 Marina, Captain Cook Drive
departure_points.detail: Base for marina-berthed charter boats, e.g. Reef Fish & Dive 1770's Southern Comfort.

departure_points.name: Beach at the 1770 Camping Grounds
departure_points.detail: Hooked On 1770 collects guests by tender from this beach at 6am and returns them there.

departure_points.name: Round Hill Creek bar
departure_points.detail: The creek is very shallow and the bar shifts constantly (it has moved hundreds of metres over the years). At low tide there can be as little as about a foot of water over it. Boaties are advised to plan around the tide, plot their outbound track on GPS for the return, and log plans with VMR Round Hill. The Queensland boating chart advises contacting VMR Round Hill before entering and crossing only in daylight without local knowledge. Hooked On 1770's booking calendar flags days when the 6am or 4pm tide is below the safe creek-entrance height.

grounds.name: Inshore deep-water reefs (within ~15 nm of 1770)
grounds.detail: Hooked On 1770's main grounds: nannygai, sweetlip, cod, cobia, mackerel, hussar and parrot, plus red emperor and coral trout.

grounds.name: 15 Mile Reef and 20 Mile Reef
grounds.detail: Closer reefs for various reef species when not doing the longer run to the Bunker Group.

grounds.name: Bustard Head rocks
grounds.detail: North along the coast off Bustard Head (lighthouse), rocks rise from about 100 ft of water: mackerel, tuna, trevally, snapper in season, and bottom fishing.

grounds.name: Trawler wrecks off the 1770 coast
grounds.detail: Cobia, tuna, trevally, cod and occasional reef fish all year round.

grounds.name: Lady Musgrave Island
grounds.detail: The closest Bunker Group reef, at the group's southern end. Fishes well on the eastern side (coral trout and red throat emperor from ~15 m; red emperor beyond 40 m). Its lagoon is an overnight anchorage reached by a deep-water channel. Sharks can be a problem in the warmer months.

grounds.name: Boult and Hoskyn reefs
grounds.detail: North of Lady Musgrave. The 50-100 m country on the eastern side holds red throat emperor, parrot, trout, cod and red emperor, with big pearl perch (~6 kg) out toward the 100 m line.

grounds.name: Fitzroy Reef
grounds.detail: Fished on the eastern side, where small isolated pinnacles in 60-100 m can hold schooling red emperor of 10-15 kg (generally May-October), plus trout, red throat and amberjack. The lagoon is a second overnight anchorage, but the entrance is narrow and shallow, so enter in daylight.

grounds.name: Lamont Reef
grounds.detail: Near Fitzroy. Fishes on the northern and western sides in 5-30 m for parrot, red throat emperor and trout, sometimes with schools of 6-8 kg red emperor.

grounds.name: Capricorn and Bunker Group (overall)
grounds.detail: Straddles the Tropic of Capricorn at the southern end of the GBR, 45-75 km from the departure ports of Yeppoon, Gladstone, Town of 1770 and Bundaberg. The visitor centre gives the closest reef as about 30 miles offshore. A 1770-Musgrave-Fitzroy loop is a 2-3 day trip of 200+ km for private boats.

grounds.name: Creeks and estuaries: Round Hill, Eurimbula, Middle, Jenny Lind and Pancake creeks
grounds.detail: Barramundi, queenfish, mangrove jack, trevally, estuary cod, grunter, silver and pike bream, Burnett salmon, flathead and whiting. Eurimbula Creek is a mud crab sanctuary.

grounds.name: Baffle Creek (south of Agnes Water)
grounds.detail: A 120 km waterway between conservation parks with sand flats, rock bars and mangroves: over 77 fish species recorded, including bream, whiting, flathead, grunter, salmon, cod, jewfish, barramundi, mangrove jack, queenfish, trevally and tarpon. The mouth is shallow and snaggy. Boat ramps at Flat Rock, Winfield and the Ferry Crossing.

grounds.name: Beach and rock fishing
grounds.detail: Rock spots include the 'catwalk' at Agnes Point and Wreck Rock. Bream, dart and sweetlip are caught, plus Spanish and spotted mackerel, mac tuna, giant herring, golden and giant trevally, cobia, queenfish, black jew, kingfish and tailor. Beaches give dart, jew, bream, tarwhine, whiting, flathead and shark. Some spots need a 4WD.

species_seasons.detail: Schools of 10-15 kg fish on isolated pinnacles east of Fitzroy Reef.

species_seasons.species: Reef fish generally (coral trout, red throat emperor, red emperor)
species_seasons.detail: Offshore reef fishing 'fires up' as water cools and currents slow. The author keeps Lady Musgrave for the cooler months because sharks take hooked fish in warmer months.

species_seasons.species: Coral Trout, Sweetlip, Red Emperor, Spanish Mackerel
species_seasons.detail: The visitor centre lists these as the main offshore catches around Fitzroy Lagoon, Boult and Lamont reefs and Lady Musgrave.
Around the trawler wrecks off the 1770 coast.

species_seasons.when: In season; closed 15 July-15 August 2026 statewide
species_seasons.detail: Taken off Bustard Head in season. Snapper and pearl perch are closed in all Queensland tidal waters 15 Jul-15 Aug.
Found in the local creeks. No take, and no catch-and-release targeting, during the closed season.

rules.rule: Most of the 1770 offshore grounds are in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park. The area has many green (no-take) zones and restricted areas, mostly on the western side of the Bunker Group. Check the current GBRMPA zoning map (Map 18, Capricorn Bunker Group); a map at the ramp is not enough on its own.

In green zones you can't fish or collect, but you may swim, snorkel, boat and transit with fish on board, as long as gear is stowed out of the water. Free zoning maps are available from bait and tackle shops, QPWS and GBRMPA (1800 990 177).

Coral reef fin fish spawning closures for 2026 run 8-12 October and 6-10 November. They cover tidal waters from Cape York south to latitude 24 50' S, so they include 1770 (about 24 10' S; position from Wikipedia coordinates).
Barramundi closed season on the Queensland east coast runs 1 November to 31 January.
Snapper and pearl perch closed season in all Queensland tidal waters runs 15 July to 15 August (2026).
Eurimbula Creek is a mud crab sanctuary.
GBRMPA has fined anglers for fishing a no-take zone in the southern Capricorn Bunker Group during a fishing competition (four people, about $14,500 in total).

getting_there.detail: Drive: from Brisbane 479.9 km / about 5 h 30 min; from Bundaberg 122.2 km / about 1 h 25 min; from Gladstone 123.8 km / about 1 h 30 min; from Rockhampton 224.9 km / about 2 h 33 min.
Fly: the nearest airports are Gladstone and Bundaberg, mostly via Brisbane; then hire car or pre-booked Agnes Water/1770 taxi and shuttle.

Bus and train: Greyhound runs daily to Agnes Water (stop at the Ampol, corner Round Hill Rd and Captain Cook Dr). The Tilt Train and Spirit of Queensland stop at Miriam Vale, 54.7 km (about 40 min) away.
The Town of 1770 sits on a peninsula with the Coral Sea and Bustard Bay on three sides; the boat ramp and marina are on Captain Cook Drive.

notes.detail: History: the town stands on the site of James Cook's second landing in Australia (and first in what is now Queensland), on 23 May 1770. Originally called Round Hill after its creek, it was renamed in 1936. A re-enactment is held each May at the 1770 Festival.

The fishing is shaped by the Round Hill Creek bar: charter departure and return times are set by the tide, and private boats need local knowledge and good fuel reserves for the long runs to the Bunker Group.
Lady Musgrave's lagoon can be entered via a deep-water channel and is the most heavily used camping island in the group thanks to its protected anchorage. Day boats run from 1770 and Bundaberg.
Heavy tackle is recommended on the Bunker Group reefs so fish come up before sharks take them. Drift fishing with a para-anchor is the usual approach.
Town facilities for anglers include a large tackle shop, supermarket, fuel and ice; some rentals offer boat storage and filleting tables.

faq.q: How far out is the reef from 1770?
faq.a: The visitor centre gives the closest reef as about 30 miles offshore. The Capricorn and Bunker Group lies 45-75 km from the departure ports. Hooked On 1770 also fishes deep-water reef country within about 15 nautical miles of 1770.

faq.q: How much is a full-day fishing charter from 1770?
faq.a: As of October 2026, Hooked On 1770 charges $450 per person for a full day and $320 for a half day, with gear and bait supplied (BYO food). Reef Fish & Dive 1770 lists a full day at $400 per person including gear and food (confirm with the operator).

faq.q: Why do charter times depend on the tide?
faq.a: Boats leave through Round Hill Creek, where the bar is shallow and keeps moving. Operators check the tide height at departure and return, and VMR Round Hill can give current bar information.

faq.q: When is the best time for reef fishing?
faq.a: Local anglers rate the cooler months highest: reef fishing picks up as the water cools, and red emperor school on the Fitzroy pinnacles generally from May to October. Note the coral reef fin fish closures in October and November.
Yes, within Queensland size and bag limits. Reef Fish & Dive 1770 asks guests to bring an esky and can arrange a local filleting service.

faq.q: Do I need to bring fishing gear?
faq.a: Not on the day charters. Hooked On 1770 supplies rods, reels, bait and tackle, and Reef Fish & Dive 1770 supplies Shimano gear.

faq.q: Can I fish around Lady Musgrave Island?
faq.a: Parts of it. The Bunker Group has many green (no-take) zones, so check GBRMPA Zoning Map 18 before fishing. Charter skippers fish the open zones.

departure_points.name: Gladstone Marina, Bryan Jordan Drive
departure_points.detail: Departure point for Gladstone's liveaboard reef fishing charters (Eastern Voyager departs from The Pier, Bryan Jordan Drive). Gladstone has direct access to Heron, Wilson and Curtis islands from the marina.

departure_points.name: Night Crossing check-in, 6 Beckinsale St, Gladstone
departure_points.detail: Check-in point for MV Night Crossing trips, with free lock-up car parking.

grounds.name: Rock Cod Shoal
grounds.detail: The closest reef stop for most anglers out of Gladstone, 8-25 m deep but exposed in wind: trout, sweetlip, cod and other reef fish, plus the odd tuna and mackerel.

grounds.name: Masthead Island
grounds.detail: Sheltered anchorage and national-park camping island. Reef-edge fishing for trout, with red emperor on isolated shoals to the north and mackerel trolled in deeper water off the edges.

grounds.name: Wistari Reef
grounds.detail: Further out and less fished. Red throat emperor are prolific, with some coral trout. Part of the reef is green zone.

grounds.name: Heron Island and Sykes Reef
grounds.detail: Heron is about 80 km from Gladstone and largely green zone. Sykes Reef, the outer reef about 120 km out, has coral trout, red throat and Spanish mackerel.

grounds.name: Capricorn and Bunker Group
grounds.detail: Island and reef chain about 80 km east of Gladstone, much of it in the Capricornia Cays National Park. Mikat runs minimum 3-day trips here and to Douglas Shoals, and Eastern Voyager runs 4-6 night trips.

grounds.name: Swain Reefs and Saumarez Reef
grounds.detail: About 120 nautical miles offshore, reached overnight. This is the main destination of Gladstone's week-long liveaboards, fished from dories for coral trout and red throat emperor, among other species.

grounds.name: Coral Sea reefs (Marion, Frederick, Kenn, Wreck)
grounds.detail: About 200 nm offshore; 10-day minimum trips.

grounds.name: Shoalwater Bay and Island Head Creek
grounds.detail: Listed as alternative destinations on Gladstone liveaboard itineraries.

species_seasons.species: Coral Trout, red throat emperor (Sweetlip), Red Emperor
species_seasons.detail: Main reef targets on Capricorn Bunker and Swains trips. Closed during the coral reef fin fish closures (8-12 Oct and 6-10 Nov 2026).
Mikat's trip report describes the start of September as the peak of the Swains season.
Trolled in deeper water off the reef edges in the Bunker Group.

rules.rule: Coral reef fin fish closures for 2026 run 8-12 October and 6-10 November (Cape York to 24 50' S, which includes Gladstone and the Swains).
Heron Island is largely green zone and parts of Wistari Reef are green zone. Check GBRMPA zoning maps for the Capricorn Bunker Group and the Swains before fishing.
On liveaboards that fish from self-drive dories (e.g. Night Crossing), you need a recreational ship master (boat) licence to drive a dory; any Australian state or territory licence is accepted.
Barramundi closed season 1 Nov-31 Jan; snapper and pearl perch closed 15 Jul-15 Aug (2026).

getting_there.detail: Gladstone is 517 km by road north-west of Brisbane and 108 km south-east of Rockhampton. Night Crossing quotes about 6 hours' drive (about 600 km) from Brisbane.
Direct flights Brisbane-Gladstone take about 1 hour. Gladstone Airport is about 6 km (8 minutes) from the city centre, and a taxi from the airport to the boat takes about 10 minutes.
From Agnes Water: 123.8 km, about 1 h 30 min by road.

notes.detail: Gladstone's reef fishing charters are almost all multi-day liveaboards (3 to 10+ days) to the Capricorn Bunker Group, Swains and Coral Sea. They typically clean, process and freeze the catch for guests to take home.
Swains fishing charters out of Gladstone were pioneered from the 1970s by the Gleeson family (Night Crossing).
Gladstone is Queensland's largest multi-commodity port and Gladstone Harbour lies within the Great Barrier Reef World Heritage Area.
Tura Charters, a long-time Gladstone liveaboard operator, is no longer operating.

faq.q: Are there day fishing trips from Gladstone?
faq.a: Very few. The only one found was Gladstone Fishing Charters and Eco Tours, listed with the Queensland visitor centres association: an 11-hour day on a Kevlacat 2400 around the Capricorn Bunker Group for up to four anglers, with gear, bait and lunch supplied. Its current trading status couldn't be confirmed, so it isn't listed.

faq.q: How long are Gladstone reef fishing trips?
faq.a: Night Crossing runs Friday-to-Thursday Swains trips. Mikat runs a minimum of 3 days (Capricorn Bunker) and 7-10 days for the Swains. Eastern Voyager runs 4 to 10+ nights. Coral Sea trips need about 10 days.

faq.q: Do I need to bring my own fishing gear?
faq.a: It depends on the boat. Mikat asks guests to bring all personal fishing gear (starter bait supplied). Check with each operator.

faq.q: Can I take my fish home?
faq.a: Yes. Gladstone liveaboards such as Night Crossing and Mikat process, package and freeze the catch, within bag limits.

faq.q: Can I snorkel or dive on a fishing liveaboard?
faq.a: Not on all of them. Night Crossing is fishing only (no scuba, spearfishing or snorkelling), while Mikat suggests bringing snorkelling gear.
